delegations.answer:
PARTIAL ANSWER: The affected S3 bucket is **frothlywebcode**. Two `PutBucketAcl` events were found, both targeting this single bucket by user `bstoll`:

| eventID | eventTime | bucketName | user |
|---------|-----------|------------|------|
| ab45689d-69cd-41e7-8705-5350402cf7ac | 2018-08-20T13:01:46Z | frothlywebcode | bstoll |
| 9a33d8df-1e16-4d58-b36d-8e80ce68f8a3 | 2018-08-20T13:57:54Z | frothlywebcode | bstoll |

No `PutBucketPolicy` or `PutBucketWebsite` events were found in the CloudTrail data — only `PutBucketAcl` (2 events) appeared among S3 write operations. All other S3 events were read-only (GetBucket* operations). Only one bucket name (`frothlywebcode`) appears in the PutBucketAcl events, suggesting only one S3 bucket was made publicly accessible.

UNCERTAINTY: I was unable to read the raw event bodies to confirm the specific ACL grant details (e.g., whether the grants include `AllUsers` URI `http://acs.amazonaws.com/groups/global/AllUsers` or `AuthenticatedUsers`, or a canned ACL like `public-read` / `public-read-write`). The `requestParameters` nested fields containing the ACL grant details were not fully extracted in my aggregation query before I reached the tool call limit.
